rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The frog is dioecious, contrasting with the hermaphrodite earthworm. The male's yellowish testes sit on the kidneys; sperm travel through vasa efferentia and the kidney's Bidder's canal along the shared urino-genital ducts to a seminal vesicle and the cloaca.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Male: testes → vasa deferentia → seminal vesicles → cloaca
Female: ovaries → oviducts (jelly coat) → uterus → cloaca
Fertilisation: external (in water) during amplexus

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Frogs have EXTERNAL fertilisation (in water), NOT internal.  ·  The male does NOT have a copulatory organ; he releases sperm over the eggs during amplexus.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects labelled male and female reproductive diagrams.  ·  External fertilisation + amplexus is a very common long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Amplexus*** — the male's nuptial-pad clasp of the female during spawning.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: frog, reproductive system, male, female reproductive organs (within Faunal Diversity).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Biology — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label male reproductive system  ·  Label female reproductive system

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Testes on kidneys, sperm through the kidney — the frog's shared plumbing."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What is amplexus? **Answer.** The **mating clasp of the frog**: during the monsoon breeding bout the male grips the female's back with his **nuptial pads** (rough thumb pads), holding on — sometimes for hours — while she sheds eggs; both release gametes into the water simultaneously so **external fertilisation**…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Urino-genital duct:** in the male frog one duct serves urine and sperm — a primitive vertebrate condition retained in amphibians.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Male: testes on kidneys (mesorchium) → vasa efferentia → Bidder's canal in kidney → urino-genital duct → seminal vesicle → cloaca; shared urinary-genital duct.  ·  Female: ovaries (seasonal size) → long coiled oviducts secreting albumen and jelly → ovisacs/uterus → cloaca.  ·  Breeding: monsoon; amplexus with nuptial pads; external fertilisation in water; jelly-swollen egg masses; tadpole larva; metamorphosis — indirect development.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A female frog may release 2,000–4,000 eggs in one spawning — overproduction in action.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Frog fertilisation is: → B  ·  The male's grip on the female during reproduction is called: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Dioecious Amphibian Reproduction Unlike the hermaphrodite earthworm, the frog is **dioecious** — separate sexes with distinct organs — and fertilisation is **external**: eggs and sperm are shed into water. This topic covers the male and female reproductive organs and their roles in breeding.  ·  ## 2. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Development: zygote → blastula → gastrula → tadpole → metamorphosis → adult  ·  Amplexus: male grasps the female (axillary in Rana, inguinal in some frogs) to coordinate egg and sperm release.  ·  The oviduct adds a jelly coat to the eggs; the jelly protects the eggs in water.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Tadpoles have gills + tail; adults have lungs + no tail (metamorphosis).  ·  The testes are kidney-shaped and lie along the dorsal body wall; the ovaries are lobed and also on the dorsal wall.  ·  Distinguish between key concepts in Protista and Protozoa.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Understand the differences between similar topics.  ·  Practice identifying the correct application of principles.  ·  The tadpole-to-adult metamorphosis sequence is a frequent exam topic.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Frogs as bio-indicators (skin absorption of pollutants) is an application question.  ·  Pay attention to key terminology in Protista and Protozoa.  ·  Connect this topic to other biological concepts.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Distinguish the frog (dioecious, external, indirect) from the earthworm (hermaphrodite, internal, direct) — a favourite comparison.  ·  "External fertilisation trades protection for numbers."  ·  Why does the frog's ovary change size through the year? **Answer.** The ovary is **seasonal**: it swells enormously before the monsoon as thousands of ova mature and fill it with yolk, then shrinks to a small resting organ after spawning empties it.…
